The search turned up consistent guidance on writing `SKILL.md`, mostly from third-party guides plus one Anthropic blog post. Its excerpt was mostly example lists, so I'd treat Anthropic's official docs and the `anthropics/skills` repo as the primary references.

- **The description drives triggering.** Claude reads each skill's description at session start and picks the matching one, so most writing effort belongs there. One guide says vague descriptions can mean a skill never activates (Claude reads every skill's description at session start and fires the one that matches your request.; The description is how Claude discovers your Skill. A vague description means the Skill will never be activated.).
- **Keep the body lean.** Put essentials in `SKILL.md` and move detailed references into support files, with scripts for utilities (SKILL.md: Essential information, quick start, navigation. Support files: Detailed references, examples, patterns. Scripts: Utilities that are executed without loading the code into context). One guide notes that at startup only the name and description of each skill are loaded. The full SKILL.md only gets read when relevant.
- **One skill, one job.** Small, focused skills are recommended over broad ones (One skill, one job — small and focused beats broad and vague). One guide also suggests stating when not to use a skill, e.g. a negative trigger.
- **Restrict tools when appropriate.** The `allowed-tools` frontmatter field can limit what a skill may do, such as read-only auditing (Use allowed-tools to restrict capabilities).
- **Scripts only when needed.** One guide advises adding scripts only when instructions alone prove unreliable (Add scripts only when markdown instructions alone are unreliable.).
- **Versioning and distribution.** Version team-shared skills in git, and package a skill as a plugin once you want to share it. Skills are the unit of capability; plugins are the unit of distribution.
- **Testing.** Verify a skill actually fires and behaves as intended before relying on it. Use `/skills` to list loaded skills and their sources.

Caveat: the sources are secondary guides, and some are repeated mirror copies of the same page. The "2026" dates are unverified, so check Anthropic's official docs for current specifics like frontmatter fields.

content.text:
## Best practices for writing Claude Code skills

The search results were mostly third-party guides, plus Anthropic's engineering post and a Claude blog post. I didn't find Anthropic's official authoring best-practices page, so check the current docs for exact frontmatter fields and limits.

**1. Put most of your effort into the description.**
- Claude loads only each skill's name and description at startup. It uses them to decide whether to open the skill.
- A vague description means the skill may never trigger. Say what the skill does and when to use it.
- Some guides suggest adding negative triggers, meaning when *not* to use it.

**2. Use progressive disclosure.**
- Keep `SKILL.md` to the essentials: a quick start and pointers to other files.
- Put detailed references, examples and patterns in separate support files. Claude reads them only when needed.
- Scripts can run without their code being loaded into context.

**3. One skill, one job.** Small, focused skills work better than broad ones.

**4. Add scripts only when needed.** Use them when written instructions alone aren't reliable enough, such as for deterministic steps.

**5. Restrict tools where it makes sense.** The `allowed-tools` frontmatter field can limit what a skill may do. A read-only audit skill is one example.

**6. Test it.**
- Check that the skill actually fires on the prompts you expect.
- Check that it behaves correctly once it does.
- `/skills` lists loaded skills and where they came from.

**7. Version and distribute deliberately.** Keep team skills in git. Package them as plugins when you want to share them more widely.

**Caveat:** These are secondary sources, and some are mirrors of the same page. I can fetch Anthropic's official docs and the `anthropics/skills` repo to confirm the details if you'd like.

Sources:
- [How to create a Claude Code skill (and the best practices nobody put in the docs)](https://codemeetai.substack.com/p/how-to-create-a-claude-code-skill)
- [Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills](https://claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills)
- [Claude Code Skills best practices (designrevision)](https://designrevision.com/blog/claude-code-skills-best-practices)
- [Claude Code Skills: The Complete Guide](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/149/claude-code-skills-complete-guide-automation-development)
- [Engineering at Anthropic: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)
- [Agent Skills: Progressive Disclosure as a System Design Pattern](https://www.newsletter.swirlai.com/p/agent-skills-progressive-disclosure)
